# Closed-minor quotas force an occupied-parity center outside every face

This is an exact finite arithmetic lemma. It uses only positive base
weights, lattice completeness and the closed-minor quotas. Concavity of
fiber-volume roots, convex fiber compatibility and mixed cap geometry
are NOT required. The stronger conclusion is base depth at least M/k,
not merely Gamma_d M/k or M/(2k).

It refines the maximal-threshold proof in
`candidate 58dcf29bfb78a573`
by retaining the parity classes of the points allowed to survive inside
a specified face. In particular it does not presume the false inequality
k(P outside F)<=k(P)-k(P intersect F).

## 1. Definitions and theorem

Let Lambda be an affine lattice and let

    P=conv(P) intersect Lambda

be finite and nonempty. Put Q=conv(P). Let k be the number of parity
classes of P modulo twice the direction lattice. Give each p positive
weight V_p and write

    V(T)=sum_(p in T) V_p,       M=V(P),       alpha=M/k.

A nonempty subset T of P is a CLOSED MINOR if

    P intersect conv(T)=T.

Its parity count k(T) uses the inherited lattice. Define closed-halfspace
base depth at p by

    delta(p)=min_(closed affine H containing p) V(P intersect H).

In positive affine rank the whole-space trace may be allowed without
changing the minimum. In rank zero it is the sole trace. All minima are
attained because there are finitely many halfspace traces of P.

**Theorem.** Fix a nonempty proper face F of Q. Suppose

    V(T)<=k(T) M/k                                             (1)

for EVERY nonempty closed minor T contained in P intersect F. Then
there is an actual p in P outside F with

    delta(p)>=M/k.                                            (2)

Thus the user's stronger hypothesis of strict quotas for EVERY proper
closed minor implies (2) outside EVERY proper exposed face. Even the
nonstrict face-local quotas (1) suffice. Faces of a polytope are exposed,
but the proof uses just the defining face property of a segment.

For an empty excluded face, (2) is the ordinary occupied-parity weighted
center theorem and the same proof below applies with no surviving points.
There is no nonempty proper face in rank zero, so that case is vacuous.

## 2. The finite maximal-threshold construction

Suppose, contrary to (2), that every p in P outside F has delta(p)<alpha.
Choose one closed halfspace H_i containing each such p, with

    H_i={x:a_i(x)>=b_i},       V(P intersect H_i)<alpha.        (3)

The index list is finite and nonempty, and a_i are affine linear.
The complementary open system a_i(x)<b_i has no point of P outside F.
Choose finite upper bounds

    U_i>max(b_i, max_(p in P) a_i(p)).

Consider the threshold box with the closed exclusion condition

    B={c: b_i<=c_i<=U_i for all i,
           for every p in P outside F there is i with
                                      a_i(p)>=c_i}.           (4)

This set is nonempty because b belongs to it, and compact because its
conditions are a finite intersection of finite unions of closed sets
inside a bounded box. Choose c in B maximizing sum_i c_i. Call an index
nonsaturated if c_i<U_i; let J denote these indices and r=|J|.

For every i in J there exists a WITNESS p_i in P outside F such that

    a_i(p_i)=c_i,       a_j(p_i)<c_j for every j!=i.            (5)

Indeed consider the outside points that strictly satisfy all other
inequalities. Condition (4) makes their ith inequality a_i(p)>=c_i.
If equality never occurs, finiteness supplies a uniform positive gap
(or there are no such points). Increasing c_i slightly then keeps
(4) and c_i<U_i, contradicting maximality. This proves (5).

Let the surviving trace of the open system be

    T={p in P:a_i(p)<c_i for every i}.                         (6)

It is contained in F by (4). If it is nonempty, it is a closed minor:
conv(T) is contained in the SAME open convex intersection, so every
point of P in conv(T) already belongs to T. It is proper because
F is proper and P outside F is nonempty.

Saturated inequalities a_i(x)<U_i are satisfied by all points of P.
Consequently the expanded closed bad caps

    G_i={x:a_i(x)>=c_i},       i in J,

cover P outside T. Each G_i is a subset of H_i, and hence

    V(P intersect G_i)<alpha.                                (7)

At least one index is nonsaturated: otherwise every outside point
would strictly satisfy every inequality, violating (4).

## 3. The parity loss includes the surviving face trace

The witnesses p_i have pairwise distinct occupied parities. If p_i,p_j
had the same parity, their actual midpoint m would be in Lambda and in
conv(P), hence in P. Since both endpoints are outside the face, m is
outside F: membership of an interior segment point in a face would
force BOTH endpoints into that face. For every inequality, (5) gives
strict satisfaction at the midpoint, contrary to (4).

More strongly, NONE of the witness parities is occupied by T. If
p_i and t in T have the same parity, their midpoint again belongs to P.
One endpoint is outside F, so the midpoint is outside F. At inequality
i, one endpoint has equality and the other is strict; at every other
inequality both are strict. The midpoint therefore strictly satisfies
all inequalities, again contradicting (4).

With k(empty)=0, these two statements give the exact bound

    r+k(T)<=k.                                                (8)

This does not count ALL parities outside F. It counts only the finitely
selected maximal-threshold witnesses and proves their disjointness from
the ACTUAL surviving trace. This is the essential arithmetic distinction.

## 4. The mass contradiction, including all closed boundaries

If T is empty, (7) and (8) give

    M <=sum_(i in J) V(P intersect G_i)<r alpha<=k alpha=M,

which is impossible. If T is nonempty, the same cover gives

    M-V(T)<r alpha<=(k-k(T))alpha,

and therefore

    V(T)>k(T)alpha.                                           (9)

This contradicts (1), proving the theorem.

All bad caps are CLOSED and include their boundary atoms. The
complementary system is OPEN precisely so that (5) and the strict
midpoint arguments are valid. No boundary weight is discarded.
There are no limits of lattice points, weights, or selected normals.

## 5. An exact alternative without any quota hypothesis

The same argument gives a useful finite certificate. For ANY tau>0,
if every p outside F has delta(p)<tau, then the construction produces
a closed trace T contained in F, possibly empty, and r witnesses with

    r+k(T)<=k,
    M-V(T)<r tau<=(k-k(T))tau.                                (10)

The set T cannot have k(T)=k, since M-V(T)>0. Equivalently, either
there is an outside point of depth at least tau, or an actual closed
minor T contained in F satisfies

    V(T)>M-(k-k(T))tau,       k(T)<k.                          (11)

For T empty this is interpreted literally as 0>M-k tau. In particular,
setting tau=M/k makes T nonempty and forces the precise quota violation
(9). The witness construction, rather than a comparison of k(F) with
k(P outside F), supplies the certificate.

## 6. Consequences and retained scope

Under the global nonstrict proper-minor quotas, the set

    D={p in P:delta(p)>=M/k}

is not contained in ANY proper face of Q. Equivalently its minimal
containing face is Q, and conv(D) meets the relative interior of Q.
This does not assert that D itself contains a relative-interior lattice
point; even an empty lattice simplex illustrates that distinction.

If an affine multiplier ell is nonnegative on Q and vanishes exactly
on a proper face F, some p with ell(p)>0 has delta(p)>=M/k. Thus any
separate limiting argument that makes the buffered depth at such p
approach its actual base depth has a strict reserve over Gamma_d M/k
for d>=1. Establishing that limiting convergence is a separate geometric
step; it is not presumed by this finite theorem.

The proof also works for any finite labeled set with the property that
the midpoint of two distinct equally labeled points belongs to the set,
with k occupied labels. The midpoint need not retain that label. This
extension uses exactly the two midpoint contradictions in Section 3.
No arbitrary finite real base without midpoint closure is covered.
